source: Independent published regimental history + NY State Military Museum / Phisterer unit summary

entries.title: Richard Eddy, History of the Sixtieth Regiment New York State Volunteers (Philadelphia, 1864)
entries.method: Fetched full djvu OCR text (809,434 chars); scanned for Hubbell variants + color/Color Guard/Lookout Mountain.

candidates.verbatim: Company "H." ... Guiniup, A. A.  Hubbell, A. F.  Huckins, J. A.  Howes, A. S. ...
candidates.ocr_note: Clean. Confirms A. F. Hubbell in Co. H at organization.

candidates.context: Casualty list for the assault on Lookout Mountain (Nov 24 1863; narrative pp. ~307-309, 'Hooker had been ordered to take Lookout Mountain'), printed pp. 309-310; '60th lost 37 in killed and wounded'.
candidates.verbatim: Private Sidney Rider, Co. "H" ... Sergeant A. F. Hubbell, [Co. H] ... Corporal W. Tees.
candidates.ocr_note: Wound column is OCR-misaligned, so the SPECIFIC wound text cannot be reliably tied to Hubbell's row; what is certain is that Sergeant A. F. Hubbell, Co. H, appears among the 60th's Lookout Mountain WOUNDED.
candidates.significance: INDEPENDENT corroboration (rubric C9) of (a) Co. H membership and (b) the family's 'wounded at Lookout Mountain' tradition. Eddy is a separate published witness from the AG roster.

entries.color_bearer_note: Eddy mentions color-bearers/Color Guard only generically (e.g. Cedar Mountain 'Four of the Color Guard were shot down') and does NOT name Hubbell as a color-bearer. The color-bearer role remains a family-record claim, not externally corroborated (open → handoff).
entries.second_hubbell: NONE — both Hubbell hits are the same man, A. F. Hubbell of Co. H.
entries.claude_reasoning: C1 + C9: independent published source places A. F. Hubbell in Co. H AND names Sergeant A. F. Hubbell in the Lookout Mountain wounded list, matching the roster's rank and the family's wound tradition. Lifts identity from 'likely' to 'confirmed' as a genuinely independent corroboration.

entries.title: NY State Military Museum 60th Infantry historical sketch (drawing on Phisterer, New York in the War of the Rebellion)

key_facts.organization: Organized at Ogdensburg; mustered in for three years Oct 30 1861 under Col. William B. Hayward; left the State Nov 4 1861.
key_facts.company_H_recruitment_verbatim: Company H was recruited principally at 'Champlain, Mooers, Ellenburgh, Altona, Chazy, Saranac and Lisbon.' (Champlain first-listed — matches Alexander's enlistment 'at Champlain' and birthplace.)
key_facts.brigade_corps: 12th Corps, Second Division, Third Brigade (Gen. George S. Greene at Gettysburg); later consolidated into the 20th Corps (Army of the Cumberland / Georgia).
key_facts.battle_list: B&O Railroad guard; Shenandoah; Second Bull Run; Antietam; Chancellorsville; Gettysburg (Culp's Hill, extreme left of 12th Corps); Lookout Mountain; Ringgold; Resaca; New Hope Church; Peach Tree Creek; Atlanta campaign; March to the Sea; Carolinas; Bentonville.
key_facts.gettysburg_verbatim: 'about half a mile to the right of Cemetery Hill, on Culp's Hill, the Sixtieth connecting with the right of the First Corps.' … 'At Gettysburg, 11 were killed and 39 wounded.'
key_facts.lookout_mountain_verbatim: 'at Lookout Mountain, 37 were killed and wounded (the Sixtieth capturing one cannon and battle flag).'
key_facts.muster_out_verbatim: 'Honorably discharged and mustered out, July 17, 1865, at Alexandria, Va.' (corroborates the roster's July 17 1865 — see muster-out discrepancy).

entries.claude_reasoning: C4 (strong): Co. H recruited principally at Champlain corroborates the hometown lock. Corroborates the battle arc (Culp's Hill, Lookout Mountain) and independently fixes muster-out at July 17 1865. Names no individuals — unit context only.

notes: Eddy (1864) is the high-value INDEPENDENT corroboration; the NYSMM/Phisterer sketch is unit-level color. Together they confirm Co. H, the Champlain recruitment, the Lookout Mountain wound, and muster-out July 17 1865.
